output.summary: KEP-4939 adds an optional flat `mode` field (TLS / Plaintext) to the gRPC probe's GRPCAction so kubelet can connect to gRPC health servers over TLS without verifying certificates. Status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: The gRPC probe only supported plaintext, so servers that require TLS could not be probed natively and users stayed on exec probes. The chosen design is a flat `mode` enum rather than a boolean or nested tls struct, because reviewers wanted room for future verification options without a breaking API change. The probe does not validate certificates, so the KEP treats certificate verification as a non-goal.

alternatives.option: Nested `tls` struct with `mode` field (NoVerify) on GRPCAction
alternatives.why_not: Rejected by reviewers because the probe never validates certificates, so a nested struct adds unnecessary complexity. The readme notes a flat mode field is simpler and sufficient.
Rejected in favor of a string enum so connection types can be named explicitly and future values can be added without a breaking change. Thockin argued boolean flags are generally a bad idea.

alternatives.option: Auto-detect TLS versus plaintext instead of explicit config
alternatives.why_not: bowei questioned whether auto-detection is needed, noting that always auto-detecting may leave errors in server logs from probes sending unexpected requests. The thread later says bowei resolved the question in favor of explicit config.

alternatives.option: No KEP; just ignore certificate errors (sergeykanzhelev's suggestion)
alternatives.why_not: kkoch986 and the thread concluded that a TLS-on/off option is needed, because a TLS server rejects a plaintext client and vice versa. The source does not record a formal rejection of the no-KEP idea.

evidence.quote: Add a new optional `mode` field alongside `port` and `service` in the [Probe GRPCAction]
This was rejected in favor of a string enum (`mode`) to allow explicit naming of the connection type
Always having auto-detect may leave errors in the log files of the server because you sending it things it doesn't understand
The only open question was around the API design (explicit TLS config vs auto-detection), which @bowei resolved in favor of explicit config.
